packet.headline_seed: More than 800 Canadian wildfires burning as air quality alerts extend to US
packet.description_seed: The air quality in large parts of Michigan, Minneapolis and Minnesota is deemed "hazardous" by authorities.

what: More than 800 Canadian wildfires burning as air quality alerts extend to US

clean_source_blocks.text: Smoke from the wildfires is causing poor air quality across New York City, with hazy skies captured on Wednesday More than 800 wildfires are burning across Canada, with air quality alerts now extending south into multiple US states. The air quality in large parts of the northern states of Michigan, Minneapolis and Minnesota is deemed "hazardous" by the US Air Quality Index program, with people recommended to stay indoors. Alerts span the Upper Midwest, the Great Lakes region and into the US's Northeast, the US's national weather service (NOAA) said in an update on Thursday. There are currently 857 fires actively burning in Canada, including 23 new fires on Thursday, according to the Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Centre. Watch: Orange haze from Canada wildfires seen in Ontario and northern US
The air quality in large parts of Michigan, Minneapolis and Minnesota is deemed "hazardous" by authorities.

Canadian wildfires are again affecting the skies – and air quality – across the United States. Smoke wafting southward from hundreds of active fires in Canada on Wednesday, July 15, led to yellow, brown and hazy skies from the Great Lakes region to the Northeast. Making matters worse were numerous fires burning in northern Minnesota along the border with Canada. The National Weather Service had issued dense smoke advisories for northern Michigan, and air quality alerts were in effect from northern Michigan, northern Illinois and central Indiana into much of New York, Massachusetts and New Jersey. "Smoke from Canadian wildfires is expected to reach New Jersey later this evening, affecting our air quality," New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill posted on X on Wednesday, July 15. "Sensitive individuals should limit time spent outdoors and avoid strenuous activity."

According to the Canadian Wildland Fire Information System, the vast majority of wildfires are burning out of control. The large cluster of fires affecting western areas of Ontario are responsible for sending thick plumes of smoke and poor air quality across Thunder Bay and Toronto, with lower concentrations of smoke high in the atmosphere drifting over the Great Lakes and above New York with hazy skies and redder sunrise and sunsets likely. There will be quite widespread thunderstorms in Ontario over the next few days, but the rain may not be enough to make much of a difference. Northwesterly winds will continue to blow the smoke into northern US states for the rest of this week and into the weekend, leading to concerns smoke will drift into New Jersey where Sunday's World Cup final is due to take place.

payload.title: Kanadan maastopalojen savu heikentää ilmanlaatua laajalti Yhdysvalloissa
payload.summary: Kanadassa palaa 857 aktiivista maastopaloa. Savu on heikentänyt ilmanlaatua Yhdysvaltojen pohjois- ja koillisosissa, ja haitan arvioidaan jatkuvan viikonlopulle.
payload.content:
Kanadassa oli torstaina 16. heinäkuuta yhteensä 857 aktiivista maastopaloa, joista 23 oli uusia. Paloista leviävä savu on heikentänyt ilmanlaatua laajalla alueella Yhdysvaltojen pohjois- ja koillisosissa. Ilmanlaatu on luokiteltu vaaralliseksi Michiganin ja Minnesotan laajoissa osissa, myös Minneapolisissa, ja ihmisiä on kehotettu pysymään sisätiloissa.

## Varoituksia Suurilta järviltä itärannikolle

Yhdysvaltain kansallisen sääpalvelun torstaisen tilannepäivityksen mukaan ilmanlaatuvaroitukset ulottuvat Keskilännen pohjoisosista Suurten järvien alueen kautta maan koillisosaan. Keskiviikkona 15. heinäkuuta Kanadasta kulkeutunut savu värjäsi taivasta kellertäväksi ja ruskeaksi sekä aiheutti laajaa utuisuutta Suurten järvien seudulta kohti koillista. Savu sumensi taivasta myös New Yorkissa.

Michiganin pohjoisosiin annettiin varoituksia tiheästä savusta. Ilmanlaatuvaroituksia oli voimassa myös Illinoisin pohjoisosissa, Indianan keskiosissa sekä laajoilla alueilla New Yorkissa, Massachusettsissa ja New Jerseyssä. Tilannetta pahensivat Kanadan palojen lisäksi lukuisat maastopalot Minnesotan pohjoisosissa lähellä Kanadan rajaa. New Jerseyn kuvernööri Mikie Sherrill kehotti herkkiin väestöryhmiin kuuluvia rajoittamaan ulkoilua ja välttämään raskasta rasitusta.

## Valtaosa paloista ei ole hallinnassa

Kanadan virastojen välisen metsäpalokeskuksen mukaan maassa paloi torstaina 857 aktiivista maastopaloa. Kanadan metsäpalotietojärjestelmä arvioi valtaosan paloista olevan hallitsemattomia. Erityisesti Länsi-Ontarion suuri palokeskittymä on lähettänyt paksuja savupilviä Thunder Bayn ja Toronton alueille, joilla savu on heikentänyt ilmanlaatua.

Pienempinä pitoisuuksina savu on kulkeutunut korkealla ilmakehässä Suurten järvien ja New Yorkin ylle. Se voi aiheuttaa utuisen taivaan lisäksi tavallista punertavampia auringonnousuja ja -laskuja. Pohjoisesta kulkeutuva savu yhdistyy Yhdysvaltojen puolella Minnesotan palojen päästöihin, mikä lisää savuhaittaa etenkin maan pohjoisosissa.

## Savun kulkeutuminen jatkuu viikonlopulle

Ontarioon ennustetaan lähipäivinä laajoja ukkosalueita, mutta niiden tuomat sateet eivät välttämättä riitä muuttamaan palotilannetta merkittävästi. Luoteistuulten odotetaan kuljettavan savua Yhdysvaltojen pohjoisosiin loppuviikon ja viikonlopun ajan. Savun pelätään leviävän jälleen New Jerseyyn, jossa maailmanmestaruusturnauksen loppuottelu on määrä järjestää sunnuntaina. Ilmanlaadun kehitys riippuu palojen lisäksi tuulten suunnasta ja siitä, kuinka paljon Ontarion ennustetut sateet hillitsevät paloja.

article.source_text:
Smoke from the wildfires is causing poor air quality across New York City, with hazy skies captured on Wednesday More than 800 wildfires are burning across Canada, with air quality alerts now extending south into multiple US states. The air quality in large parts of the northern states of Michigan, Minneapolis and Minnesota is deemed "hazardous" by the US Air Quality Index program, with people recommended to stay indoors. Alerts span the Upper Midwest, the Great Lakes region and into the US's Northeast, the US's national weather service (NOAA) said in an update on Thursday. There are currently 857 fires actively burning in Canada, including 23 new fires on Thursday, according to the Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Centre. Watch: Orange haze from Canada wildfires seen in Ontario and northern US

The air quality in large parts of Michigan, Minneapolis and Minnesota is deemed "hazardous" by authorities.

Canadian wildfires are again affecting the skies – and air quality – across the United States. Smoke wafting southward from hundreds of active fires in Canada on Wednesday, July 15, led to yellow, brown and hazy skies from the Great Lakes region to the Northeast. Making matters worse were numerous fires burning in northern Minnesota along the border with Canada. The National Weather Service had issued dense smoke advisories for northern Michigan, and air quality alerts were in effect from northern Michigan, northern Illinois and central Indiana into much of New York, Massachusetts and New Jersey. "Smoke from Canadian wildfires is expected to reach New Jersey later this evening, affecting our air quality," New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill posted on X on Wednesday, July 15. "Sensitive individuals should limit time spent outdoors and avoid strenuous activity."

According to the Canadian Wildland Fire Information System, the vast majority of wildfires are burning out of control. The large cluster of fires affecting western areas of Ontario are responsible for sending thick plumes of smoke and poor air quality across Thunder Bay and Toronto, with lower concentrations of smoke high in the atmosphere drifting over the Great Lakes and above New York with hazy skies and redder sunrise and sunsets likely. There will be quite widespread thunderstorms in Ontario over the next few days, but the rain may not be enough to make much of a difference. Northwesterly winds will continue to blow the smoke into northern US states for the rest of this week and into the weekend, leading to concerns smoke will drift into New Jersey where Sunday's World Cup final is due to take place.
